**Coaching note (78 words):**
When the enemy king is trapped by its own pawns, look for forcing checks that drive it into tighter corners. Here, Qh8+ is a quiet-sounding move that looks like just another check, but it forces Black's king to g5—the only legal square. Then Qh4 is checkmate because the king has no escape: g6 is blocked by its pawn, f4 and f5 are controlled by the queen, and h5/h6 are also covered. Weak kings on the side of the board are vulnerable to queen checks that restrict their movement.
